explain.say: Imagine all the rubbish your home makes in a week piled up in your bedroom. Yuck! But lots of it is not really rubbish at all: it can be turned into new things. Let's sort it into the right bins.

explain.say: See Paper and card lighting up? Newspapers, cereal boxes and egg boxes can be mashed up with water and made into new paper and card. Keep them dry and clean. How many cardboard boxes does your home use in a week?

explain.say: Now Plastic and metal glows. Plastic bottles, drinks cans and food tins can all be recycled. Give them a quick rinse first so they do not make other things dirty. Can you find something plastic that could be recycled near you?

explain.say: Here are Food scraps. Banana peels, eggshells and tea leaves can rot down into compost, a dark, crumbly soil food that helps plants grow. Worms and tiny decomposers do all the work! Do you know anyone with a compost heap?

explain.say: And here is a plastic bottle's journey: sorted, shredded, melted, then made into new things, even fleece jackets. Glass goes in its own bin and can be recycled again and again forever. Super sorting, Earth helper! Remember: reduce, reuse, then recycle.

stages.label: New things
stages.ask: What happens to a plastic bottle after recycling?

faq.a: Most paper and card, many plastic bottles and pots, drinks cans and food tins, and glass bottles and jars can be recycled. Rules differ between towns and countries, so check your local bins.
asks: Which things go in the recycling?

faq.q: What happens to a plastic bottle after recycling?
faq.a: It is sorted by type of plastic, washed, shredded into flakes and melted into pellets. The pellets are made into new bottles, clothes like fleeces, or things like benches.
Compost is rotted-down food scraps, leaves and grass. Worms, fungi and bacteria break them into dark, crumbly material that feeds plants.
Recycling saves raw materials like trees, oil and metal ores, uses less energy than making things new, and keeps rubbish out of landfill sites and the sea.

faq.q: What does reduce, reuse, recycle mean?
faq.a: Reduce means use less, like carrying a reusable bag. Reuse means use things again, like refilling a water bottle. Recycle means turn old things into new materials. Reducing and reusing are even better than recycling.

facts: Glass can be recycled again and again without losing quality.
Recycled PET plastic bottles are often made into polyester fibre for clothing such as fleece.
